newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-CZECHS CAPITALISE ON GERMAN WEAKNESSES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CZECHS CAPITALISE ON GERMAN WEAKNESSES.

text.p: Germany, without injured top players Steffi Graf and Anke Huber, lost their Fed Cup world group one tie to the Czech Republic on Sunday after suffering defeat in both reverse singles.
The results earned the Czechs a semifinal tie against the Dutch after Marlene Weingaertner and Barbara Rittner proved unable to fill the huge gap left by Graf and Huber.

The 23-year-old Rittner, unused to her temporary role as German number one, got the day off to a bad start, losing 6-1 6-4 to Ludmila Richterova, 19, who had stepped in for leading Czech player Jana Novotna, suffering from shingles.
The match appeared over for Rittner after just 18 embarassing minutes as Richterova took five games in a row.
Rittner pulled back one game but blew any chance of a recovery in the second set by missed numerous chances.
Weingaertner, 17, who pulled off a surprise victory over Richterova on Saturday, could not keep up her form on Sunday and lost 6-2 6-2 to Adriana Gersi to give the Czechs the tie.
German coach Klaus Hofsaess said that, despite the result, he could see Weingaertner developing into an important player for her country.
